meta.description: Canonical content of the Neo4j knowledge graph: one FCC unit, 22 assets, 10 Management of Change records and their work orders, hazards, risk assessments and outcomes. Synthetic research data.
meta.provenance: Converted from a Neo4j Browser export of the project database dated 2026-05-08, merged with the two nodes that existed only in the live database on 2026-11-12. Dates are ISO strings. Duplicate relationships removed.

props.change_description: It is proposed that to solve the excessive vibration and deteriorating performance of the feed preparation area P-101 feed pump, the replacement should be done. Although the new pump is likely to enhance reliability and energy efficiency, it will not change the characteristics of feed flow including pressure, flow rate, and stability.
props.description: Replace failing feed pump P-101 with upgraded unit
props.engineering_risks: Temporary instability in flow during start-up or switch-over. Lack of correspondence with current control valve features. Possible oscillations in flow control loop FIC. Threat of reactor temperature fluctuation due to variations in feed flow rate and composition.
props.hazop_justification: HAZOP not required: Like-for-like pump replacement with no change to process design limits, control philosophy, or operating envelope; existing HAZOP remains valid. PSSR required: installing new equipment prior to start-up.
props.hazop_reason: Like-for-like replacement, no change to process design limits
props.lessons_learned: Improved pump reliability and stable operation
props.name: MoC-001
props.system_impacts: P-101 directly feeds reactor R-201. Any variation in flow stability can affect reactor inlet conditions including flow and temperature coupling, catalyst reaction efficiency, and downstream fractionator load and separation performance.
props.title: Feed Pump (P-101) Replacement

props.change_description: The modification of the FV-103 control valve to a smart control valve will enhance the temperature regulation process in the feed heater. The change will also bring about advanced control such as remote control and improved feedback accuracy.
props.description: Replace FV-103 with smart control valve to improve temperature regulation and enable remote monitoring
props.engineering_risks: Incorrect tuning of PID leading to temperature control oscillation. Sensor-actuator mismatch leading to delayed control system response. Integration errors in control systems commissioning. Threat of overheating or under heating of the reactor feed.
props.hazop_justification: HAZOP required: impact on important temperature control loop. PSSR required: because of instrumentation and control logic revision.
props.lessons_learned: Enhanced temperature control after tuning stabilization
props.name: MoC-002
props.parameter_name: Temperature control accuracy and response time
props.reason: Inconsistent control performance and need for improved temperature stability
props.system_impacts: The feed heater directly influences reactor inlet temperature. It influences the reaction kinetics of catalyst in R-201, influences the yield of products and selectivity, and influences the downstream separation in the fractionator.
props.title: Feed Heater Control Valve (FV-103) Upgrade

props.change_description: The change in reactor temperature R-201 setpoint is a system-level change in the FCC Unit, and its effects spread over several interrelated regions. Reactor temperature change has a direct impact on reaction kinetics in the Reactor-Riser and consequently the catalyst activity, regenerator heat equilibrium and the subsequent separation of product downstream in the Fractionation section. This interdependency brings about the element of complexity since changes in temperature can affect the feed conversion efficiency, distribution of product yield and stability in operation. Besides, the change also affects control loops that control temperature, flow, and pressure, which enhances the chances of coupled system responses.
props.description: Adjust reactor temperature setpoint to optimise catalyst performance and improve gasoline yield
props.engineering_risks: Heat build-up and deactivation of catalysts in reactors. Bigger coke growth that influences the performance of the regenerators. Existence of thermal imbalance between reactor and regenerator. New operating range instability of control loop.
props.hazop_justification: HAZOP mandatory: alteration of critical process parameter. PSSR required: prior to working within new conditions.
props.lessons_learned: Improved yield with stable thermal control
props.name: MoC-003
props.reason: Need to improve catalyst activity and process efficiency
props.system_impacts: Directly impacts catalyst activity and coke formation. Influences regenerator load via coke burn-off. Affects downstream product distribution in fractionator. Interacts with air blower and combustion control system.
props.title: Reactor R-201 Temperature Setpoint Adjustment

props.change_description: Inspection and repair of the internal components of the C-203 cyclone separator to address erosion damage and restore separation efficiency. The repair restores the cyclone to its original design condition without changing process design basis or operating limits.
props.description: Inspect and repair cyclone internals to restore catalyst separation efficiency
props.engineering_risks: Downstream fouling due to the leakage of catalysts. Reactor performance changes due to pressure drop changes. Failure to repair completely results in a recurrence of failures. The risks of start-up following shutdown.
props.hazop_justification: HAZOP not required: Repair restores the cyclone separator to its original design and operating condition, with no change to process design basis, control philosophy, or operating limits. PSSR required: owing to the shutdown and the opening of important units.
props.hazop_reason: Repair restores original design, no change to operating limits
props.lessons_learned: Restored separation efficiency and reduced losses
props.name: MoC-004
props.reason: Erosion damage causing catalyst losses and reduced efficiency
props.system_impacts: Ineffective separation will result in carryover of catalyst to fractionator. Modifies load of regenerator and emissions. Affects mass balance of the FCC.
props.title: Cyclone Separator (C-203) Internal Inspection and Repair

props.change_description: Upgrade of catalyst control valve SV-204 with an advanced actuator is proposed to improve control of catalyst circulation between reactors and regenerator.
props.description: Upgrade slide valve actuator to improve catalyst circulation control and monitoring
props.engineering_risks: Actuator malfunction leading to uncontrolled catalyst circulation. Sensor-actuator mismatch causing delayed or inaccurate control response. Control signal or feedback loop failure reducing regulation accuracy. Interaction failure with temperature and pressure control loops. Risk of thermal imbalance across the FCC Unit. Potential propagation of instability across interconnected systems.
props.hazop_justification: HAZOP mandatory: modification of a critical control element governing multiple interconnected process areas, strong system coupling between reactor and regenerator, high potential for propagated system-wide effects. PSSR required: validation of actuator installation, calibration, and integration with control systems prior to commissioning.
props.lessons_learned: Improved catalyst circulation and process stability
props.name: MoC-005
props.reason: Need for improved catalyst flow control and reactor-regenerator balance
props.system_impacts: Directly regulates catalyst circulation rate between reactor and regenerator. Maintains thermal balance between Reactor-Riser and Catalyst Regeneration. Influences reactor conversion efficiency and product yield. Affects regenerator combustion stability and heat generation. Interacts with temperature, pressure, and flow control loops. Represents a critical coupling point between reaction and regeneration systems.
props.title: Catalyst Slide Valve (SV-204) Control System Upgrade

props.change_description: This scenario proposes enhancing stripping efficiency in the catalyst stripper S-301 by installing a steam flow control valve and optimizing the steam injection rate.
props.description: Install steam control valve and optimise steam injection to improve stripping efficiency
props.engineering_risks: Excessive steam injection causing temperature imbalance. Insufficient stripping leading to hydrocarbon carryover and potential afterburn in the regenerator. Control loop instability due to improper tuning of steam flow regulation. Leakage risk at valve connections or flanges during commissioning. Potential disturbance propagation across interconnected process sections.
props.hazop_justification: HAZOP required: direct impact on stripping efficiency and regenerator combustion behavior, interaction with thermodynamic balance and process emissions, involvement of control system modification affecting process stability. PSSR required: verification of valve installation, integrity, and control loop performance prior to startup.
props.lessons_learned: Steam leakage incident required improved flange installation and inspection procedures
props.name: MoC-006
props.reason: Improve stripping efficiency and reduce hydrocarbon carryover
props.system_impacts: Stripping efficiency directly affects hydrocarbon carryover to the regenerator. Increased carryover impacts regenerator combustion load and emissions. Influences overall heat balance across the Reactor-Riser and Catalyst Regeneration sections. Affects downstream flue gas treatment and environmental compliance. Interacts with temperature and flow control loops within the FCC Unit.
props.title: Catalyst Stripper Steam Optimization

props.change_description: Modification of flue gas expander EX-403 to enhance the level of energy recovery by installing modern turbine gear.
props.description: Upgrade expander components to improve energy recovery and operational efficiency
props.engineering_risks: Expander trip with accumulation of pressure in regenerator. More flaring because of bypass activation. Mechanical misalignment, vibration and failure. Connection with the pressure control system.
props.hazop_justification: HAZOP not required: upgrade remains within existing process design limits and control philosophy, with no change to normal operating envelope. PSSR required: before commissioning upgraded expander.
props.hazop_reason: Upgrade within existing process design limits
props.lessons_learned: Temporary misalignment caused trip. Improved alignment procedures implemented
props.name: MoC-007
props.reason: Low efficiency and opportunity for improved energy recovery
props.system_impacts: Expander transforms pressure into regenerator by energy recovery. Has an impact on regenerator pressure balance and flue gas flow. Downstream emission control systems are affected. Associated to air blower and combustion stability.
props.title: Flue Gas Expander (EX-403) Performance Upgrade

props.change_description: To prevent frequent breakdowns in the functioning of the reflux pump and increase the stability of the fractionation process, replacement of reflux pump P-502 is offered.
props.description: Replace reflux pump P-502 to improve reliability and stabilize fractionation process
props.engineering_risks: Column instability related to the column equilibrium. Poor sizing of pump leads to imbalance. Transients in startups which influence product quality. Communication with level and temperature control loops.
props.hazop_justification: HAZOP required: influences the performance of separation and quality of product. PSSR required: required before the start-up after the pump changed.
props.lessons_learned: Alignment issues required improved installation and startup procedures
props.name: MoC-008
props.reason: Frequent failures affecting separation performance
props.system_impacts: The reflux flow has a direct influence on the column separation efficiency. Affects purity of products and recovery. Modifies temperature and pressure of the influencer. Associated with upstream product composition of reactor.
props.title: Fractionator Reflux Pump Replacement

props.change_description: The emergency shutdown ESD procedure for the FCC Unit is revised following a safety audit to improve response time, communication protocols, and coordination between control room and field operators during emergency conditions.
props.description: Revise FCC emergency shutdown procedure and train operators
props.engineering_risks: Delayed shutdown due to incorrect or incomplete procedure execution. Miscommunication between operators during critical conditions. Failure or misalignment of safety interlocks and automated shutdown logic. Human-machine interface errors affecting response accuracy. Increased risk severity during emergencies due to procedural gaps or delays.
props.hazop_justification: HAZOP mandatory: direct impact on safety-critical operations and shutdown logic, involvement of human-control system interaction, potential for system-wide consequences across the FCC Unit. PSSR required: verification of updated procedures, operator readiness, and system integration prior to implementation.
props.lessons_learned: Improved emergency preparedness and response coordination
props.name: MoC-009
props.reason: Improve response coordination and communication after safety audit
props.system_impacts: ESD activation affects all major subsystems within the FCC Unit including Reactor-Riser, Catalyst Regeneration, and Fractionation. Requires coordinated interaction between control room systems and field operators. Involves safety interlocks, shutdown logic, and alarm management systems. Integrates multiple instrumentation and control systems across process areas. Depends on synchronized execution across interconnected units.
props.title: Emergency Shutdown Procedure Update

props.change_description: Installation of high-temperature resistant materials to reinforce the catalyst transfer line between the reactor and regenerator in order to deal with any wear and enhance long-term integrity.
props.description: Reinforce catalyst transfer line to improve integrity and prevent failure
props.engineering_risks: Loss of containment due to line failure. Blockage of the catalyst flow causing instability of the process. Defects that undermine integrity because of welding. Thermal stress caused by high operating temperatures.
props.hazop_justification: HAZOP mandatory: important mechanical integrity and continuity of the process. PSSR required: prior to reinforced line re-commissioning.
props.lessons_learned: Weld defect required rework. Improved welding and inspection procedures implemented
props.name: MoC-010
props.reason: Material degradation and wall thinning identified
props.system_impacts: Reactor and regenerator critical link. Influences the circulation of catalysts and continuity of the processes. It affects body temperature and response rate. It may significantly affect the overall performance and stability of the FCC Unit.
props.title: Catalyst Transfer Line Reinforcement
